title: If on Our Daily Course Our Mind
description: If on Our Daily Course Our Mind in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Keble wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 304, “Seeing God in All”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: If on our dail-y course our mind Be set, to hal-low all we find, New trea-sures still, of count-less price, God will pro-vide for sac-ri-fice.

lines: If on our daily course our mind
Be set, to hallow all we find,
New treasures still, of countless price,
Old friends, old scenes, will lovelier be,
As more of heaven in each we see;
Some softening gleam of love and prayer
Shall dawn on every cross and care.
O could we learn that sacrifice,
What light would all around us rise!
How would our hearts with wisdom talk
The trivial round, the common task,
Will furnish all we ought to ask;
Room to deny ourselves, a road
To bring us daily nearer God.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Keble died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Keble (1792–1866), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
